Known science foundations of Computational Universe Reconstruction.

Simulation-based inference recovers cosmological parameters from survey data (DES, Planck). Normalizing flows and neural posterior estimation invert complex simulators in particle physics. Digital-twin methods reconstruct unobservable states in engineering. Extending this to hidden physical structure (dark sector, early universe) is theoretically motivated but unverified.

Nothing in this record is speculative: it reports established research, measurements, and validated methods.

Physical and engineering constraints on Computational Universe Reconstruction.

Inverse problems are often ill-posed with non-unique solutions. Reconstructions inherit the biases of their simulators. Hidden structure may be fundamentally unobservable.

Scale analysis across 3 quantities spans 16.7 orders of magnitude; the dominant scale separation is hidden-sector parameters vs inference compute per analysis at 16.7 orders of magnitude (inference compute per analysis larger). Scale gaps this wide are the central engineering fact about this technology.
